description: Human-authored ContextIQ repository tasks. Queries intentionally avoid the expected symbol names where practical, so the corpus measures retrieval rather than string matching. `expected_symbols` and `must_contain` make this an answer-quality corpus: a pack passes only if it actually carries what an answer would need.

cases.task: keep caller relationships intact when only the called file changes during an incremental refresh
decide how much of each symbol to include so the answer fits a token budget
work out how many tokens a developer would have spent grepping and reading around each hit instead
report how much was saved compared with the alternative way of getting the same coverage
stop a heavily-referenced utility from crowding out the code the question was about
avoid sending the model text it was already given earlier in the same conversation
record which pieces of context have been delivered to a conversation so far
tell whether a snippet has changed since it was last handed over, ignoring reformatting
identify which vector space the stored similarity data belongs to
turn a piece of text into a fixed-length numeric signature without any model
throw away similarity data that was produced by a different model than the one now in use
find which indexed definitions still need a similarity signature computed
fetch the similarity model ahead of time so a query never stalls on a download
arrange the outgoing message so the provider can reuse most of it between requests
split the generated project overview into the part that rarely changes and the part that changes every commit
combine two differently-ordered result lists into one ranking
rank definitions by closeness in meaning rather than exact spelling
drop a snippet that repeats something already shown further up
count how many other definitions touch each one, in a single database round trip
shrink a pasted crash dump or build log before it is charged for
make sure credentials never leave the machine inside returned context
work out the size of a chunk of text the way a specific vendor's model would
price a request before it is actually sent anywhere
connect an AI client to the local code graph over the model context protocol
check whether an editor's configuration file genuinely points at this server or merely exists
decide whether to invoke the installed program or fall back to running the script directly
update a steering document without destroying the notes a human wrote in it
judge whether the retrieved material is enough to answer correctly
fail the build when retrieval quality drops below an agreed floor
score the tool against several different codebases and roll the numbers up
list everything that would be affected if a particular definition changed
show every declaration in a file without any of the implementations
assemble context for exactly what an in-progress change touches
produce a reproducible artifact that an auditor could re-derive byte for byte
infer the house style of a codebase so generated files match it
drop derived in-memory state after the underlying files moved
condense a long back-and-forth into a short brief that carries the decisions forward
remove near-identical passages from a set of snippets before they are sent
verify that repository AI configuration files point to valid local resources
declare optional packages for parsing languages, serving MCP, and accurate token counts
explain practical techniques for reducing context consumed by coding assistants
instruct GitHub Copilot to use graph retrieval before opening complete files
